rules.rule: Non-test code must not use unwrap(), expect(), panic!, unchecked indexing, or overflow-capable arithmetic on values derived from config, provider output, network data, user input, or on-disk state. Return a typed error instead.
An error on a path that mutates state must be propagated or logged. Flag `let _ =`, empty Err arms, and bare catch blocks that do neither.

JSONL journal writes must be atomic per envelope and must not leave a partial line after a crash or cancellation. Locks must be released on every error path and acquired in a consistent order across call sites. Replay and compaction must not drop, reorder, or duplicate envelopes.

Heiwa normalizes provider surfaces; it does not reimplement provider internals. Flag code that hardcodes a provider's model list, quota math, auth token lifetime, or system prompt as if Heiwa owned it, instead of reading it from the provider.
New production code must not depend on archive/, apps/heiwa_hub, or treat crates/heiwa_stdb as a normal operator-facing surface. Explicit legacy repair work is exempt when the PR states that intent.

Build paths with Path/PathBuf joins, not string concatenation with '/'. No hardcoded /tmp, no assumed HOME, no assumption that a shelled-out binary exists on all of ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, and windows-latest.

A change that introduces a new system-level build dependency (a native library, or a build script that shells out to a binary such as protoc) must also add the corresponding install step to .github/workflows/ci.yml.

No credentials, tokens, API keys, or private endpoints in tracked files, .env.example, fixtures, log lines, or error strings. Provider auth material belongs behind crates/heiwa_vault. Flag log statements that print whole config structs or provider responses.

Docs, comments, log strings, and user-facing messages must not claim capability the diff does not implement — no unearned 'supported', 'wired', or parity claims, no framing apps/heiwa_app as a native desktop runtime, no web-first framing where local-first is correct.

Port 7474 is the installed product runtime. Verification of a local build must use an alternate port such as 7475. Flag scripts, tests, or docs that verify a checkout against 7474, and flag new API routes that can fall through to the SPA and return index.html on an unknown path.
